EI 123 B-3/3D Work Summary (eliminate casing pressure and set up B-3D SS for future gas lift):

1. MIRU lift boat.

2. Pulled existing 20' packoff assembly the B-3 LS at 1624' to 1648' SLM set across the top GLM.

3. Pulled and replaced the dummy valve at 1629' SLM in the top GLM.

4. Swabbed well in and casing pressure started rising slowly (dummy still had slight leak on the top GLM).

5. Ran S/L memory log and confirmed the leak was the top GLM.

6. Pulled and replaced the dummy valve at 1629' SLM in the top GLM again with new packing.

7. Bled the SICP down from 2750 psi to 0 psi.  The LS SITP = 3675 psi.

8. Casing pressure started rising slowly (dummy still had slight leak in the top GLM).

9. Ran new 40' packoff assembly the B-3 LS from 1602' to 1654' SLM across the top GLM.

10. SICP holding at 436 psi after the packoff was set.  Bled off SICP to 0 psi through a 1/2 needle valve in 25 minutes (all gas).  Had no SICP buildup in 24 hours on chart.  Packoff holding.  The B-3 LS SITP = 4000 psi.

11. Decision made to get on the B-3D SS and go ahead and install live GLV's in the top five GLM's while on location with the lift boat as the B-3D SS was starting to load up on its own and was showing signs of needing gas lift in the near future.

12. Pulled the dummy valves in the top 5 GLM's and installed lives valves at 1596' SLM (1626' MD), 2271' SLM (2295' MD), 2760' SLM (2784' MD), 3250' SLM (3273' MD), and 3768' SLM (3790' MD).

13. Bled the SICP down from 335 psi to 0 psi.  Turned the B-3 LS and B-3D SS over to production to return to flow.

14. RDMO location with lift boat.

text:
Stimulate the C2 sand with a riserless acid stimulation. This operation will be performed in order to mitigate fines migration which has caused a decline in PI. 
The well was not flowed back and shut-in. The well is stable and currently shut in, and will remain shut in until a rig workover can be performed. Both  smart  sleeves  are  closed  and  pressure  tested  to  1,000  psi  differential,  providing  an  additional  barrier to the reservoir.     
A riserless acid stimulation was performed 2/16/17-2/17/2017 and  completed pumping at 6:20 AM on 2/17/17. On the evening of 2/17/17, communication was detected between the tubing and annulus and was confirmed through further diagnostics. The lower smart sleeve was closed on 2/18/17 at 16:00 (note: the upper smart sleeve remained closed for the duration of the project), and then methanol was injected into the tubing to apply a 1,000 psi differential - during this period DHP1 (bottom hole tubing pressure) increased 1,000  psi,  however no response was seen on DHP2(upper zone) and DHP3(lower  zone), indicating the smart sleeves are sealing and have full integrity. Prior to the departure of the riserless stimulation vessel on 2/18/17‐ 2/19/17, the tree annulus cavity was pressurized to 10,000 psi. The pressure test held and an ROV inspection during the test indicated no leaks at or around the tree. A rig intervention is being planned, and the well will remain shut-in. A casing pressure departure was approved 3/3/17 for six months.

text: W&T has been conducting a Lube and Bleed program in order to reduce casing pressure on the Intermediate Casing of the OCS G 2354 HI 111 A-11 well. The program introduces heavy weighted mud to the annulus while bleeding lighter mud and gas to reduce the sustained casing pressure to a level within API RP 90 approval requirements or to zero psi. We began with 4000 psi on the annulus and have reduced the pressure to ~ 2650 psi (some of it induced) at which point the Lube and Bleed program was suspended on 5-30-14. Over the course of the Lube and Bleed program we were able to add 14.1 barrels of 17.1 #/gallon heavy mud to the annulus and swap 59.5 barrels of lighter mud to heavy mud. Our annulus mud weights have increased from an initial weight of 9.0-9.5 #/gallon up to 13.6 #/gallon.  We have initiated a pressure monitor program for the next 30 days to determine if sustained casing pressure levels warrant a departure request for SCP or whether repair action is recommended in which case a separate submittal would be required to the District.

text:
Eugene Island 208 Well J-5st

Summary of work performed from Feb. 17, 2004 to Jan. 4, 2005

Work began on Feb. 17, 2004.  Wireline was used to clean paraffin out of the tubing.  An attempt was made to run a PS plug, but it got stuck.  After fishing the plug out of the tubing, the well was flowed to clean up the tubing and a significant increase in production was observed.   Wireline plug back operations were suspended on Feb. 21 and the well was put back on production in the original Lower JM Sand.  

Wireline plug back operations were resumed on Dec. 18, 2004.  An attempt was made again to set a PS plug in the S-1 nipple at 9490 ft, but the plug stuck in the tubing at 9444 ft.  The PS plug and the setting tool string were left in the tubing with the top of the tool string at approximately 9419 ft.  Several attempts were made to fish the tool string and plug without success.  On Jan 1, 2005,  a CIBP was run and set in the tubing at 9418 ft.  Twenty-six feet of cement were dumped bailed on top of the CIBP leaving the top of the cement at 9392 ft.  The tubing was perforated from 9330-33 ft. on Jan. 4, 2005.  The upper JM Sand was then put on test.  A 7-hour test on Jan. 20, 2005 showed the well was producing 344 bopd, 81 bwpd and 2080 mcfpd on a 24/64 in. choke with a flowing tubing pressure of 920 psi.

text:
Brazos A7 Well A-4 was one of 4 wells on the Brazos A7 Platform that were previously TA?d.  This summary covers only the recent work that was done in March, 2005 to cut and proof-pull the remaining casings in preparation for platform abandonment which is planned for the summer of 2005.  

The work began on Well A-4 on 3/14/05.  The 30-inch, 20-inch, 16-inch, and 11-7/8-inch casings were torch cut and the wellheads were removed.  The 20-inch was just a short piece about 5 feet long with a bell guide on the bottom which fell down about 10 feet into the well when it was cut loose at the surface. (The 9-5/8-inch casing had already been cut and its stub removed in 2004.)  A mechanical pipe cutter was run in the hole and the 11-7/8-inch casing was cut at 25 feet BML.  The 11-7/8-inch stub dropped 4 inches and turned freely so it had to be removed before cutting the next casing could continue.  After removing the 11-7/8? stub, the 16-inch casing was then mechanically cut at 21 feet BML.  It too, fell a few inches and turned.  The 16-inch casing stub was removed from the well.  A spear was then used to pull and remove the 5-foot piece of 20-inch casing with the bell guide on the bottom of it.  The mechanical cutter was picked up again and the 30-inch casing was cut at 18 feet BML.  The cut was completed on 3/23/05.  On 3/24/05, casing jacks were used to pull the 30-inch casing up about 2 feet to prove that the cut was complete.  The 30-inch casing stub was not removed from the well.

Final abandonment is planned for June 2005 when the 30-inch casing stub will be removed along with the entire platform.  Final site clearance will be performed after the platform is removed.
